(Today through Monday)...
Issued at 130 AM EDT Tue Oct 13 2026

Today Through Wednesday.

Broad mid-level ridging centered over the Southeast expands across 
the Ohio Valley today while a deep trough digs across south-central 
Canada and the Upper Midwest. South-southwesterly boundary layer 
flow downstream of an approaching surface cold front will reinforce 
warm thermal advection across central Indiana. Forecast soundings 
indicate 850mb temperatures climbing to 16-17C with deep diurnal 
mixing up to 800mb. The combination of WAA and plenty of sun will 
allow for temperatures to rise into the upper 80s to potentially low 
90s, breaking records. Momentum transfer within the mixed layer will 
support sustained southwesterly surface winds of 15 to 20 mph with 
gusts peaking between 25 and 30 mph.

The synoptic surface cold front will decelerate Tuesday night as 
upper-level flow orients quasi-parallel to the boundary. Mesoscale 
guidance, including the HRRR and HREF members, focuses initial pre-
frontal convective development across northwestern counties after 
midnight as a 35 kt low-level jet intercepts the frontal zone. 
Instability remains largely elevated and diurnally capped, with 
MUCAPE values generally under 500 J/kg, limiting severe convective 
potential to isolated general thunder outside of a low-end threat
for gusty winds.

The frontal zone sags into central Indiana Wednesday, serving as a 
focus for precipitation as mid-level frontogenesis tightens. 
High-resolution guidance shows precipitable water values surging 
to 1.4 to 1.6 inches along the boundary, exceeding the 90th 
climatological percentile for mid-October. Right-entrance region 
upper jet dynamics and continuous moisture transport will support 
widespread rain and embedded convective clusters throughout 
Wednesday afternoon and Wednesday night. Afternoon highs Wednesday
will exhibit a marked thermal gradient, ranging from the low to 
mid- 60s in the northwest behind the front to upper 70s and lower 
80s across south-central Indiana. 

Thursday Through Monday.

A secondary shortwave rotates through the base of the deepening 
eastern longwave trough Thursday, inducing a weak wave of low 
pressure along the stalled baroclinic zone over the Ohio Valley. 
Strong multi-level deformation and mid-level FGEN combined with deep 
moisture will maintain high PoPs through Thursday evening before the 
boundary finally clears the forecast area to the southeast. Multi-
model ensemble consensus aligns with WPC guidance depicting 
widespread event-total QPF between 1.00 and 2.00 inches across 
central Indiana, providing much-needed drought relief. 

Cold air advection strengthens drastically Thursday night into 
Friday behind the frontal passage as an amplified 500mb polar trough 
settles over the Great Lakes and eastern CONUS. An intense surface 
pressure gradient between the departing low and a 1028mb Canadian 
surface high will combine with steep low-level lapse rates to 
promote deep boundary layer mixing on Friday. Sounding profiles show 
35 to 40 kt winds at the top of the mixed layer, which will easily 
translate to surface gusts of 35 to 40 mph throughout Friday 
afternoon. Highs on Friday will be held in the mid-50s to near 60F
despite clearing skies as a result of the strong CAA. 

The core of the thermal trough crosses the region Friday night into 
Saturday, with 850mb temperatures dropping to between -2C and 
0C. Highs Saturday will struggle to reach the low to mid-50s 
under cold northwest flow. The primary frost/freeze window remains
Saturday night into early Sunday morning. The Canadian surface 
anticyclone settles directly over the Ohio Valley by 09Z Sunday, 
resulting in clear skies and a decoupled wind field. Radiational 
cooling within this dry continental airmass will cause surface 
temperatures to drop into the low to mid-30s across central 
Indiana. Widespread frost appears likely across rural and 
sheltered areas, with a localized freeze probable in typically 
colder drainage basins.

The surface ridge axis shifts toward the Mid-Atlantic on Sunday and 
Monday, allowing low-level flow to veer to the south-southwest. 
Height rises aloft downstream of a Western trough will promote 
thermal moderation, returning highs to the lower 60s Sunday and 
upper 60s by Monday under dry conditions.
